patterns.title: Mutex acquisition and release transfer an Iris resource
patterns.property: Given is_lock lk R, successful acquisition establishes locked lk ∗ R, so the holder receives both the exclusive held-lock token and the protected proposition. The companion release contract requires is_lock lk R ∗ locked lk ∗ ▷ R and returns True while restoring the unlocked lock invariant. The lock invariant stores R only in the unlocked state; locked lk is represented by fractional heap ownership of the lock flag.
hypotheses: The proof section is instantiated with heapGS Σ and lock namespace N; R is an iProp Σ.
Acquisition postcondition is locked lk ∗ R.
Release requires is_lock lk R ∗ locked lk ∗ ▷ R and returns True.
alloc_lock requires full ownership of a free lock and ▷ R to associate the lock with its invariant.

source_to_proof_to_check.property: wp_Mutex__Lock maps is_lock lk R to locked lk ∗ R; wp_Mutex__Unlock returns the held resource to the invariant and establishes True.
definitions_and_supporting_lemmas: lock_inv stores a bool flag with fractional heap ownership and R in the unlocked state.
is_lock packages the lock location and invariant; locked packages the held flag and its 3/4 points-to fraction.
wp_Mutex__Lock is derived from wp_Mutex__Lock' and wp_Mutex__TryLock, which retries until the compare-exchange succeeds.
wp_Mutex__Unlock is derived from wp_Mutex__Unlock', whose compare-exchange changes the flag to false and restores lock_inv.
locked_exclusive rules out two simultaneous held-lock resources.
source_to_proof_to_check.implementation_connection: The selected file exports the Goose lock implementation from lock.impl. The proof operates on its Mutex__Lock and lock.release expressions; the lock implementation source itself was not part of the retained six-file source bundle.
dependencies: Iris proof mode, invariants and algebra
Perennial weakest-precondition and Goose language modules

patterns.title: Crash-aware critical section preserves normal and crash resources
patterns.property: For a non-value expression e and a crash lock carrying R/Rcrash, with_lock_spec runs e while holding the lock. On normal completion, e establishes Φc ∧ Φ #() and returns R; on crash, e establishes Φc ∗ Rcrash. The enclosing WPC concludes with Φ normally and Φc on crash.
hypotheses: The proof section is instantiated with heapGS Σ, stagedG Σ and lock namespace Nlock.
The critical-section expression satisfies to_val e = None.
is_crash_lock lk R Rcrash stores crash_borrow R Rcrash in the lock invariant.
The supplied WPC for e requires R and has normal postcondition (Φc ∧ Φ #()) ∗ R and crash postcondition Φc ∗ Rcrash.
The enclosing WPC for with_lock lk e has normal postcondition Φ and crash postcondition Φc.
patterns.normal_postcondition: Φc ∧ Φ #() for the critical section, retaining R; Φ for the enclosing with_lock WPC.
patterns.crash_postcondition: Φc ∗ Rcrash for the critical section; Φc for the enclosing with_lock WPC.

source_to_proof_to_check.property: with_lock_spec preserves the exact supplied WPC outcomes while sequencing lock.acquire, e, and lock.release.
definitions_and_supporting_lemmas: is_crash_lock is an ordinary lock whose protected proposition is crash_borrow R Rcrash.
crash_locked contains the crash borrow, lock invariant and locked token.
use_crash_locked opens the crash borrow for e and returns the borrow on the normal path or Rcrash on the crash path.
with_lock is lock.acquire followed by e and lock.release; with_lock_spec composes wp_Mutex__Lock, use_crash_locked and wp_Mutex__Unlock.
